New refrigeration method stretches and squeezes metal to cool the air without compressors. (x-post from /v/Efficiency)

At a high level, this is the same as a normal air conditioner/refrigerator, except you're compressing and expanding metal instead of some sort of liquid/gas. The fundamental carnot cycle limit on efficiency still applies, and though there's still a lot of room between the theoretical limit and the efficiencies achieved in practice, it's unclear to me why this would be expected to be more efficient than usual methods. It seems the motivation may be more to eliminate the environmental cost of manufacturing and disposing of the refrigerants this would replace with nickel-titanium.
